articles.title: The Mealtime Habit That Could Secretly Be Causing Friction Between Couples
articles.summary: It’s normal to navigate life at a different pace, but this one reaction may be a red flag.
articles.body:
For some couples, eating a meal together may be where their compatibility ends. While one person scarfs down a meal, another may take leisurely bites in what is known as an "eating speed" gap.

These "eating speed" differences have been satirized in TikTok skits, with couples trying to match their partner's eating pace to funny results. Usually, there's one person who is noticeably slower at eating their meal, while their partner rushes to clear their plate.

"He had to wait three to four business days for the next bite," a commenter wrote after a video where one partner carefully sauces her bowl and chooses her television show before taking one bite.

And your date's eating speed could make or break your relationship, depending on how you view it. Evelyn Pechous , an associate licensed marriage and family therapist, said it's common for couples to navigate life at different paces.

"My perspective is that partners who eat at different paces may actually be more compatible than not," Pechous said. "Eating at different paces could indicate a necessary balance in the relationship where one person may move through the world more slowly while another may move with more vigor."

Ultimately, the only problem with an "eating speed" gap is if your date makes it a problem.

Like this article? Keep independent journalism alive. Support HuffPost .

An 'eating speed' gap doesn't need to be a dealbreaker, as long as you're respectful.

Matching your partner's eating speed is not important, but respecting these common differences is. Notice how your partner treats you during mealtimes, because it can tell you important information about how you will be treated in the long run.

"If they're respectful, like telling you not to rush and to enjoy your meal, then that's a positive for your relationship and a good sign to continue dating them," said Anita Chlipala , a marriage and family therapist. But "if they continually make rude or condescending comments, like telling you you're the slowest person on the planet or an idiot for not eating faster or for savoring your food, it might be time to stop dating them or reassess the viability of the relationship."

Everyone has a different relationship to food, and happier couples are open-minded when eating faster or slower has a deeper meaning for one person. "Don't make the other feel bad or wrong for how they eat," Chlipala said. "Talk about the why. It's fine if there's not a deeper reason for your eating speed, but for some, there is."

Chlipala recalled working with couples that argued over whether eating too fast resulted in less quality time together.

As an example, Chlipala described a couple eating dinner at home, where the faster eater gets up from the table right after they finish, which hurts the feelings of the slower-eating partner.

"The faster eater is ready to start cleaning, while the slower eater was hoping for connection time," Chlipala said.

Compromises can help both slow and fast eaters. If you're on a timeline, the slower eater may need to make adjustments, so you and your date can make your post-dinner show, Chlipala suggested, noting that fast eaters may need to be mindful of eating more than their fair share if they are splitting portions.

And instead of making one partner a perpetrator, reframe any concerns about how your partner eats as if you're collaborating together on a problem, said clinical psychologist Ryan Howes .

"They eat fast; that's not a crime. There is probably a reason for that, and abandoning you is probably not the intended goal," Howes said. "If you raise the concern and invite your partner to solve it with you, you have a good chance of solving the problem together."

Variety is the spice of life, and that includes watching your restaurant date inhale a burger.

"Differences like this are part of entering a relationship with another person," Howes said. "It's actually a key component of it ― we want to join with someone who is a little different than us because it adds variety and novelty to our lives."

articles.title: PMO scientist’ with fake ID at Jio World Plaza may have acted under hallucination, say cops
articles.summary: Mumbai Police suspect 24-year-old Rohan Parikh used AI tools to forge a PMO ID to enter BKC’s Jio World Plaza ahead of PM Modi’s visit; probe ongoing.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The city crime branch probing the case of a 24-year-old man carrying a fake Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) identity card to enter Jio World Plaza, BKC, ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit suspects his actions stemmed from a state of hallucination.The man, identified as Rohan Parikh, was accompanied by his private armed bodyguard, Dilip Kunde, and a friend.A team of Intelligence Bureau (IB), Research Analysis Wing (RAW) and Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) interrogated Rohan and Kunde, who is an ex-Armyman. Sources said Rohan admitted during interrogations that he had fabricated the ID card using AI tools.Initially, during inquiries, Rohan told the police he was a victim of a fake email sent by one Jai Shankar. However, the police checked with PMO’s office in Delhi, which confirmed they had not issued any such ID card and that the ID is a fake one.“During the inquiry, we were told that Rohan is a special child who turns aggressive at times and is moody. The family claims he is normal, but we will record his parents’ statements to understand him,” said a police source. “We are also planning to do his psychological analysis to understand as to what is the motive behind doing this,” he added.Rohan allegedly told investigators that he had lied about his identity and official assignment and that his intention was to show off his connections and gain praise from people around him and flaunt his purported connections.His digital identity card, which he flashed from his mobile phone, appears to have been forged using AI tools.Parikh was arrested along with Kunde while the third accused is on the run. Parikh claimed he was a scientist on a special assignment from Prime Minister’s Office. Police suspect that the accused had prepared forged identity cards to support his claim.Police are also examining the digital devices used by Parikh to make the fake ID cards and whether any other persons assisted him. articles.title: Married for 10 days, couple found dead in Lucknow guest house
articles.summary: Lucknow: Newlywed couple found dead in Chinhat guest house after 18-day stay; police suspect suicide by hanging, suicide note recovered, probe underway.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A 22-year-old man and a 19-year-old woman were found dead in a guest house room in Chinhat area on Wednesday night. Police said they hanged themselves from a ceiling fan hook using a dupatta. Police also recovered a suicide note from the woman’s bag.The couple had arrived from Hardoi and had been staying in a guest house in Lucknow since Aug 23. They had married on Aug 21 and the man worked at a medical store.The bodies were brought down from the hanging point and sent to RMLIMS for post-mortem. articles.title: Carro pega fogo e mãe e filha de 2 anos escapam ilesas em Vila Velha   | G1
articles.standfirst: Moradores relatam que uma forte explosão aconteceu por volta das 6h20, no bairro Alecrim. Motorista levava a filha para uma sessão de fisioterapia quando o veículo pegou fogo. Ninguém se feriu.
articles.summary: Moradores relatam que uma explosão aconteceu por volta das 6h20. Motorista levava a filha para uma sessão de fisioterapia quando o veículo pegou fogo. Ninguém se feriu.
articles.body:
Um carro pegou fogo por volta das 6h20 desta quinta-feira (10), na Rua Ana Siqueira, no bairro Alecrim, em Vila Velha, na Grande Vitória. Segundo moradores, uma mulher estava no veículo com a filha de 2 anos quando as chamas começaram. As duas conseguiram sair do carro e ninguém se feriu.

Por causa do incêndio, o veículo bloqueou uma pista da via. A Guarda Municipal de Vila Velha foi acionada e orientou motoristas. Como o movimento de veículos ainda era baixo no horário, não houve congestionamento.

Ainda de acordo com moradores da região, a motorista relatou que sentiu um cheiro forte de combustível ao sair de casa, em Cariacica. Ela levava a filha para uma sessão de fisioterapia em um hospital de Vila Velha quando o carro teria "morrido".

A mulher disse que tentou dar a partida algumas vezes. Em seguida, começou a sair fumaça e houve uma explosão.

Mãe e filha de 2 anos escapam de carro em chamas em Vila Velha, Espírito Santo — Foto: Reprodução/Rede social

Testemunhas ajudaram a apagar as chamas. Após o incêndio, o carro ficou completamente destruído.

A dona de casa, Irene Defendente, viu o momento em que mãe e filha deixaram o carro. Ela disse que a mulher comprou o veículo recentemente. Após o incidente, as duas pegaram um carro de aplicativo e deixaram o local.

“Ela ainda estava pagando o carro, que tinha comprado para levar a menina ao hospital e acabou perdendo tudo. Saiu, esqueceu de tirar os documentos, tava desorientada”, contou Irene.

A Guarda Municipal de Vila Velha foi procurada para informar as causas do incêndio e outros detalhes da ocorrência, mas não havia respondido até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: Operação contra o Comando Vermelho: MP-GO bloqueia R$ 28 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Justiça determinou o cumprimento de 10 mandados de prisão e 11 de busca em apreensão. Investigação aponta que empresas de fechada eram usadas para ocultar dinheiro obtido com o tráfico de drogas.
articles.summary: Justiça determinou o cumprimento de 10 mandados de prisão e 11 de busca em apreensão. Investigação aponta que empresas de fechada eram usadas para ocultar dinheiro.
articles.body:
Uma operação do Ministério Público de Goiás (MP-GO) contra o Comando Vermelho realizada nesta quinta-feira (10) bloqueou R$ 28,1 milhões. A ação tem como objetivo desestruturar um braço financeiro do Comando Vermelho com atuação em Goiás e no Rio de Janeiro e que teria usado contas em nomes de adolescentes para movimentar dinheiro de traficantes da organização criminosa.

Os nomes dos investigados não foram divulgados.

Operação contra o Comando Vermelho bloqueia R$ 28 milhões — Foto: Divulgação/MP

Em parceria com a Rotam, o Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco) realizou a segunda fase da Operação Cifra Vermelha . Além do valor bloqueado, a Justiça também determinou a apreensão de automóveis e bens de luxo.

Segundo o órgão, a Justiça determinou o cumprimento de 21 mandados três cidades goianas e em Minas Gerais (MG).

Veja as cidades onde os mandados foram determinados:

De acordo com a investigação, pessoas ligadas ao Comando Vermelho em Goiás abriam diversas empresas de fachada e usavam contas abertas nos nomes de adolescentes para movimentar valores depositados por traficantes.

Integrantes da organização orientavam traficantes a depositar o dinheiro nas contas dessas empresas fantasmas e de "laranjas".

"A segunda fase alcança outras pessoas ligadas às lideranças, que também ocultavam dinheiro recebido de traficantes e mantinham vínculos com a facção nos estados de Goiás e do Rio de Janeiro", informou o órgão.

Na primeira fase, 11 pessoas foram denunciadas pelo Ministério Público pelos crimes de integração à organização criminosa, lavagem de dinheiro e falsidade documental. Somados, os valores apreendidos nas duas fases ultrapassam R$ 56 milhões.

Um casal identificado como líder do grupo se escondeu em uma comunidade no Rio de Janeiro após a primeira fase da operação e foi preso três meses depois.

articles.title: Processo contra PMs denunciados por executar piloto do PCC é arquivado | G1
articles.standfirst: O arquivamento ocorreu por falta de novas provas. Policiais do COD mataram os suspeitos em uma chácara entre Goiânia e Abadia de Goiás, em 2023.
articles.summary: Justiça arquivou o caso por falta de novas provas. Policiais do COD mataram os suspeitos em uma chácara entre Goiânia e Abadia de Goiás, em 2023.
articles.body:
A Justiça arquivou o processo contra Edson Luis Souza Melo Rocha, conhecido como coronel Raiado, e o tenente-coronel Renyson Castanheira Silva referente às mortes de três homens durante um tiroteio . Entre eles estava um suposto piloto do Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC). O arquivamento ocorreu por falta de novas provas.

O caso aconteceu em fevereiro de 2023, em uma chácara entre Goiânia e Abadia de Goiás . Na época, a Polícia Militar divulgou que recebeu uma denúncia de populares sobre uma movimentação anormal de aeronaves na propriedade rural, às margens da BR-060. Foi organizada, então, uma operação com oito policias, segundo a PMGO divulgou na ocasião.

Para o Ministério Público de Goiás (MPGO), Raiado e Castanheira, que eram do Comando de Operações de Divisas (COD), forjaram um confronto e mataram o piloto Felipe Ramos Morais e os mecânicos Nathan Moreira Cavalcante e Paulo Ricardo Pereira Bueno.

Edson Luis e Renyson Castanheira foram denunciados pelo Ministério Público de Goiás por homicídio — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera e Wesley Costa/O Popular

Em entrevista ao g1 , o advogado Luis Alexandre Rassi, responsável pela defesa de Castanheira, explicou que a Justiça decidiu pelo arquivamento na última terça-feira (8). A decisão foi dada no âmbito de um habeas corpus de autoria do advogado Demóstenes Torres, que representa Raiado, mas abrange tanto ele quanto Castanheira.

O g1 entrou em contato com a defesa de Raiado, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Rassi destacou que o processo já havia sido arquivado, ainda em 2023, quando a Justiça decidiu que as mortes ocorreram por legítima defesa. O arquivamento de agora se refere a uma nova denúncia ofertada pelo MPGO este ano.

De acordo com o Ministério Público, os militares chegaram a afirmar que teria acontecido uma troca de tiros e que os suspeitos estariam de frente para eles no momento dos disparos. No entanto, os laudos de exame cadavérico e pericial apontaram, segundo o MP, que eles foram atingidos pelas costas, com Felipe e Paulo tendo sido atingidos enquanto estavam caídos e rendidos no chão.

Rassi explicou que o MP também alegou que o piloto não tinha pólvora nas mãos, o que seria uma prova de que ele não teria atirado e, portanto, não teria havido confronto.

"Só que o cadáver foi lavado antes de se fazer esse exame. Então, esse exame não prova nada", disse.

Depois, um perito particular contratado pelo MP não encontrou os cartuchos do tiroteio. "O que acontece? Era um campo. Então, não vai achar mesmo. Não se acha", explicou Rassi.

Antes do habeas corpus, o advogado Rassi entrou com uma ação de "exceção de coisa julgada", argumentando à Justiça que a decisão anterior, do arquivamento, não teria como ser revertida.

"O juiz decidiu por legítima defesa, que é imutável. E você não pode julgar duas vezes uma pessoa pelo mesmo fato", disse.

Segundo o advogado, a apelação estava prevista para ser julgada nesta quinta-feira (10), mas não será mais, em função da decisão de terça.

O g1 questionou o MPGO se pretende recorrer da decisão, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Professor Wagner obtém 80,06% dos votos para reitor da Unimontes | G1
articles.standfirst: Professor já ocupa o cargo de reitor desde 2022. Para o cargo de vice-reitor, o candidato mais votado foi Dalton Caldeira Rocha, com 74,8% dos votos.
articles.summary: Professor já ocupa o cargo de reitor desde 2022. Para o cargo de vice-reitor, o candidato mais votado foi Dalton Caldeira Rocha, com 74,8% dos votos.
articles.body:
Campus da Unimontes, em Montes Claros — Foto: Unimontes/Divulgação

O professor Wagner de Paulo Santiago obteve 80,06% dos votos e foi o candidato mais votado nas eleições para a escolha da reitoria da Universidade Estadual de Montes Claros (Unimontes). Ele já ocupa o cargo de reitor desde 2022.

Em segundo e terceiro lugares na votação ficaram os professores Antônio Alvimar, com 9,5% dos votos, e Ilva Ruas, com 7,2%.

Para o cargo de vice-reitor, o candidato mais votado foi Dalton Caldeira Rocha, com 74,8% dos votos. Paulo Eduardo Gomes de Barros obteve 19,5%.

Os candidatos mais votados em cada cargo irão compor a lista tríplice, que será encaminhada ao governador de Minas Gerais. Cabe ao governador escolher, entre os nomes da lista, quem irá assumir a reitoria. Antes do envio, há prazo para interposição de recursos e análise pela Comissão Eleitoral.

Pela primeira vez, a votação no processo eleitoral da universidade foi realizada de forma on-line, por meio do sistema eletrônico SigVoto. A votação ocorreu das 8h às 22h desta quarta-feira (9).

Os votos para a escolha do reitor e do vice-reitor são paritários, com os seguintes pesos: professores (70%), servidores técnico-administrativos (15%) e acadêmicos (15%).

articles.title: Alerta de tempestade em Piracicaba: ventos de 60km/h e granizo | G1
articles.standfirst: Metrópole registrou 11,9 milímetros de chuvas até as 7h desta quinta-feira (10). A medição é da estação meteorológica do LEB, na Esalq-USP.
articles.summary: Após registrar 11,9 mm de chuva, Piracicaba entra em alerta de tempestade com risco de granizo e ventos intensos em 18 cidades da região.
articles.body:
Cidades da região de Piracicaba (SP) devem registrar máximas na casa dos 24ºC nesta quinta-feira (10). O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu alerta amarelo de risco para tempestades nos 18 municípios da área de cobertura do g1. O aviso prevê chuvas de até 50 milímetros por dia, ventos intensos de 40 a 60 km/h), e queda de granizo.

Piracicaba registrou 11,9 milímetros de chuvas até às 7h desta quinta-feira, segundo os dados da Estação Meteorológica do Departamento de Engenharia de Biossistemas (LEB), na Esalq-USP.

No acumulado dos nove primeiros dias de setembro, Piracicaba somou 46,2 mm em volume de chuvas. A média história para todo mês é de 60 mm.

Não há registros de alagamentos ou outros incidentes devido às chuvas na região até a publicação desta reportagem.

Piracicaba teve junho mais chuvoso em dez anos, aponta Esalq-USP — Foto: Claudia Assencio/g1

Capivari (SP) registrou 45 milímetros de chuvas nas últimas 24 horas. A Prefeitura de Capivari segue em monitoramento.

A orientação é para que a população acompanhe os alertas oficiais e adote medidas preventivas para minimizar os riscos durante o período de instabilidade.

Em caso de necessidade, a Defesa Civil de Capivari atende pelo 199 e pelo telefone (19) 3492-3186. A Guarda Civil atende pelo 153 e pelo WhatsApp (19) 3491-1311, 24 horas por dia, sete dias por semana. O Corpo de Bombeiros atende pelo 193.

De acordo com a previsão do Inmet, nesta quinta-feira (10), as máximas não devem ultrapassar os 25ºC.

articles.title: Achou documento perdido em Feira de Santana? Veja onde entregar | G1
articles.standfirst: Recolhimento ocorria apenas na Central de Achados e Perdidos. Local conta atualmente com cerca de 2 mil documentos aguardando retirada.
articles.summary: Recolhimento ocorria apenas na Central de Achados e Perdidos. Local conta atualmente com cerca de 2 mil documentos aguardando retirada.
articles.body:
Documentos podem ser recuperados na sede da Guarda Municipal em Feira de Santana — Foto: Jorge Magalhães/ Arquivo

Quem encontrar documentos ou objetos perdidos em Feira de Santana , segunda maior cidade da Bahia, agora poderá entregá-los em qualquer repartição pública municipal. A medida foi publicada no Diário Oficial do Município no último sábado (5).

Com a mudança, documentos e objetos encontrados pela população podem ser entregues em locais como escolas, unidades de saúde, Centros de Referência de Assistência Social (Cras), Centros de Referência Especializado de Assistência Social (Creas) e secretarias municipais. Antes, a entrega era concentrada na Central de Achados e Perdidos.

A medida também busca facilitar a devolução de pertences aos donos e ampliar os pontos onde a população pode deixar materiais encontrados.

Atualmente, a Central de Achados e Perdidos tem cerca de 2 mil documentos aguardando retirada pelos proprietários.

A Central de Achados e Perdidos funciona na sede da Secretaria Municipal de Prevenção à Violência (Seprev), na Rua Leolinda Bacelar, 224, no bairro Kalilândia, em Feira de Santana.

Para retirar o documento, o proprietário deve apresentar um documento oficial com foto para comprovar a titularidade. Caso não tenha outro documento, a identificação pode ser confirmada pelos dados e pela foto presentes no próprio documento encontrado.

O titular também precisa assinar um termo de retirada.

A retirada pode ser feita por outra pessoa, desde que o representante apresente uma autorização por escrito do proprietário.

Entre os materiais que chegam à Central estão RGs, CPFs, cartões do SUS, carteiras de habilitação (CNH) e carteiras de trabalho.

Quanto tempo os documentos ficam guardados?

Os documentos permanecem na Central de Achados e Perdidos por até 120 dias, o equivalente a quatro meses.

Segundo o coordenador do setor, Sandro Ricardo Lima, o prazo costuma ser ampliado para aumentar as chances de que os documentos sejam devolvidos aos proprietários. De acordo com ele, geralmente a devolução aos órgãos expedidores acontece apenas no final do ano.

Onde consultar se um documento foi encontrado?

A lista com os nomes das pessoas que tiveram documentos encontrados pode ser consultada no site oficial da Prefeitura de Feira de Santana.

Para consultar, o cidadão deve acessar a página da Prefeitura e clicar na opção “Serviços”. Entre os serviços disponíveis, “Achados e Perdidos” aparece logo no primeiro item. Ao acessar a página, é possível conferir a lista de pessoas que têm documentos disponíveis para retirada na Central.

Além da consulta, os moradores também podem entregar documentos e objetos encontrados na cidade em qualquer repartição pública municipal.

articles.title: Ana Castela faz ‘show particular’ em casa para família e amigos no MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Com apenas uma caixa de som e um microfone, a boiadeira soltou a voz durante uma confraternização em sua cidade natal. A cantora postou em suas redes sociais o momento.
articles.summary: Com apenas uma caixa de som e um microfone, a boiadeira soltou a voz durante uma confraternização em sua cidade natal. A cantora postou em suas redes sociais o momento.
articles.body:
A cantora sul-mato-grossense Ana Castela, improvisou um verdadeiro show durante uma confraternização com familiares e amigos em Sete Quedas (MS), cidade onde nasceu e cresceu.

Com apenas um microfone e uma caixa de som, ela soltou a voz enquanto os amigos fizeram uma espécie de plateia. O momento foi registrado pela própria cantora e publicado nas redes sociais nesta quarta-feira (9).

No vídeo, Ana aparece sentada à mesa com os convidados enquanto canta “É Que Eu Não Te Esqueci”, música lançada neste ano. Para não correr o risco de esquecer a letra, a cantora deixou o celular apoiado em um pote de doce e acompanhou a música enquanto cantava.

Os amigos também entraram no clima. Eles usaram as lanternas dos próprios celulares para iluminar o ambiente e acompanhar a apresentação improvisada.

Ana Castela com amigos e família em sua casa em Sete Quedas — Foto: Redes Socias

Em determinado momento, Ana Castela chama a 'plateia':

Na sequência, os amigos respondem aos gritos, como se estivessem diante de um grande palco.

Ana Castela está passando um período em sua casa em Sete Quedas, no sul de Mato Grosso do Sul. O vídeo publicado pela cantora rapidamente chamou a atenção dos fãs e acumulou milhares de curtidas e milhões de visualizações nas redes sociais.

articles.title: Justiça determina nova perícia sobre pousada em Pipa | G1
articles.standfirst: Processo discute desde 2006 a construção do empreendimento em área apontada como de preservação permanente.
articles.summary: Justiça determina nova perícia ambiental em pousada na Praia de Pipa, em Tibau do Sul. Processo discute construção em área de preservação permanente.
articles.body:
Praia do Amor em Pipa — Foto: Fernanda Zauli/g1

A 2ª Vara da Comarca de Goianinha determinou a realização de uma nova perícia ambiental na área onde funciona uma pousada na Praia de Pipa, em Tibau do Sul , no litoral Sul do Rio Grande do Norte. A decisão foi tomada em uma Ação Civil Pública que tramita desde 2006 e discute a construção do empreendimento em uma área apontada como de preservação permanente.

Segundo o juiz Demétrio Demeval Trigueiro do Vale Neto, o laudo produzido em 2016 apresenta fragilidades e contradições que impedem que o documento seja utilizado como fundamento suficiente para o julgamento da ação.

De acordo com o magistrado, o próprio perito havia apontado que a área do empreendimento está inserida em Área de Preservação Permanente (APP) de restinga, além de ter identificado supressão de vegetação responsável pela sustentação de dunas.

Apesar disso, o laudo anterior concluiu que a construção estaria de acordo com a legislação ambiental por ter sido licenciada pelo Instituto de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e Meio Ambiente do Rio Grande do Norte (Idema).

O juiz também contestou a conclusão de que a reparação do dano ambiental seria impossível porque a pousada já está construída e em funcionamento.

Na decisão, o magistrado citou a Súmula 613 do Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ), que impede a aplicação da chamada teoria do fato consumado em matéria ambiental.

Segundo o processo, a perícia realizada anteriormente não foi concluída porque o profissional responsável pelo trabalho morreu em 2019, antes de responder aos quesitos complementares determinados pela Justiça.

Para o juiz, a morte do perito, somada às inconsistências encontradas no documento, torna necessária a realização de uma nova avaliação técnica.

A nova perícia será feita pelo Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama). O órgão terá 60 dias para realizar a vistoria e responder aos questionamentos apresentados pelo Ministério Público do Rio Grande do Norte (MPRN).

O Ibama também deverá apresentar, em até 30 dias, cópia do processo administrativo relacionado à autorização para supressão de vegetação, além de eventuais autos de infração e termos de embargo referentes à área.

A nova vistoria deverá verificar se a área apresenta características de duna fixa e/ou restinga.

a possibilidade de recuperação ambiental em caso de demolição;

as condições para eventual recuperação da área;

medida compensatória adequada caso a recuperação seja considerada inviável.

As partes terão 15 dias para apresentar quesitos adicionais e indicar assistentes técnicos para acompanhar a vistoria.

Depois que o Ibama entregar o relatório, o Ministério Público e as demais partes serão intimados para se manifestar.

A decisão da Justiça determina apenas a realização de uma nova perícia ambiental. A possibilidade de demolição da pousada ainda será analisada posteriormente, com base nas informações técnicas que serão produzidas no processo.

O caso tramita em uma Ação Civil Pública iniciada em 2006.

articles.title: MAUAL faz 25 anos com recorde de inscrições e 103 filmes | G1
articles.standfirst: Mostra de Audiovisual Universitário e Independente da América Latina recebeu 494 produções e reúne trabalhos de 17 estados brasileiros e cinco países; programação também terá oficinas gratuitas.
articles.summary: MAUAL recebe 494 inscrições e seleciona obras de 17 estados e cinco países. Edição de 25 anos também terá oficinas gratuitas de audiovisual.
articles.body:
Edição de 2026 contou com um número recorde de inscrições — Foto: Reprodução

A 25ª edição da Mostra de Audiovisual Universitário e Independente da América Latina (MAUAL) chega com número recorde de inscrições: 494 filmes foram enviados para a seleção deste ano . Ao todo, 103 produções foram escolhidas para integrar a programação, que reúne trabalhos de diferentes regiões do Brasil e de outros cinco países latino-americanos. O evento vai acontecer dos dias 06 a 10 de outubro no Teatro da Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso (UFMT).

Entre os selecionados estão 46 curtas-metragens para a Mostra Competitiva, 51 para a Mostra Paralela e seis videoclipes. As produções representam 17 estados brasileiros, além de Cuba, Venezuela, Colômbia, Uruguai e Equador. Mato Grosso também ganha destaque, com 25 filmes selecionados.

Realizada pela Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso (UFMT), a MAUAL completa 25 anos de atividades ininterruptas e escolheu como tema desta edição “Terra em Transe, Imagens em Movimento” . A proposta faz referência ao clássico Terra em Transe, de Glauber Rocha, lançado em 1967, e busca aproximar as discussões do filme dos desafios enfrentados pela sociedade atualmente.

A seleção dos filmes foi feita por um grupo formado por oito curadores e curadoras, entre profissionais do audiovisual, professores, estudantes, servidores da UFMT e agentes culturais. O grupo avaliou produções de ficção, documentários, trabalhos experimentais e videoclipes.

Ao completar um quarto de século, a MAUAL mantém como uma de suas principais propostas dar visibilidade a produções universitárias e independentes, especialmente aquelas realizadas fora dos grandes centros de produção audiovisual.

A organização considera a mostra um espaço para ampliar a circulação de diferentes histórias, culturas e formas de produção cinematográfica. A programação também busca colocar em evidência experiências e territórios que nem sempre encontram espaço nos circuitos tradicionais do cinema.

Os filmes selecionados serão exibidos no Teatro Universitário, em uma programação que pretende apresentar ao público diferentes formas de fazer cinema e de interpretar a realidade latino-americana.

Programação terá oficinas de audiovisual

Além das sessões de cinema, a 25ª MAUAL terá atividades de formação voltadas para quem deseja conhecer ou aperfeiçoar conhecimentos técnicos na área audiovisual.

A programação expandida será realizada entre setembro e dezembro deste ano e contará com três oficinas:

“Do microfone aos Metadados”, com Yuri Kopcak;

“Gerenciamento de Mídia Audiovisual no Set”, com Pê Mutz;

“Assistência de Câmera”, com Leila Sayuri e João Pedro Régis.

A identidade visual da edição comemorativa foi desenvolvida pela multiartista Amanda Homem, responsável pela criação da logomarca e das ilustrações utilizadas na programação.

articles.title: Qual o caminho dos celulares roubados em SP; operação detalha esquema criminoso | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação do Ministério Público de São Paulo descreve uma cadeia dividida em etapas, que começa no furto ou roubo do aparelho, passa por pontos de recepção no Centro, inclui desbloqueio e desmontagem de peças e termina na revenda com aparência de legalidade.
articles.summary: Investigação do Ministério Público de São Paulo descreve uma cadeia dividida em etapas, que começa no furto ou roubo do aparelho, passa por pontos de recepção no Centro, inclui desbloqueio e desmontagem de peças e termina na revenda com aparência de legalidade.
articles.body:
Operação contra roubo de celulares em SP — Foto: Reprodução

A operação Frank Mobile, deflagrada na manhã desta quinta-feira (10) pelo Ministério Público e as polícias Civil e Militar de São Paulo, detalha o caminho percorrido pelos celulares roubados e furtados na capital.

Normalmente, esse tipo de crime acontece em segundos, mas depois da ação dos criminosos, o aparelho passa por uma complexa engrenagem que envolve diversas áreas.

🔎 A operação cumpre sete mandados de prisão e quase 90 mandados de busca e apreensão contra suspeitos de furto, roubo, receptação, adulteração e revenda de aparelhos celulares em todo o país.

Segundo o Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco), essa cadeia organizada começa na subtração do aparelho na rua e em festivais, segue para imóveis e lojas no Centro de São Paulo, passa por técnicos especializados em desbloqueio e adulteração e termina em empresas e comércios suspeitos de reinserir celulares e peças no mercado com aparência de legalidade.

A apuração é um desdobramento de investigações anteriores, como a Operação Salus et Dignitas, e reúne relatórios de inteligência, rastreamento de aparelhos, análises fiscais, dados financeiros, depoimentos de colaboradores e conversas extraídas de celulares e computadores apreendidos.

O Ministério Público divide o fluxo do esquema de celulares roubados ou furtados em quatro núcleos interdependentes ( detalhes no infográfico abaixo ):

Núcleo 1 (subtração): é a ponta mais visível, com a participação dos autores de furtos, roubos e outros crimes patrimoniais envolvendo celulares;

Núcleo 2 (receptação e invasão) : é o primeiro destino dos aparelhos, segundo a investigação;

Núcleo 3 (desbloqueio) : entram técnicos, assistências e pontos comerciais apontados como responsáveis por resetar aparelhos, remover bloqueios, adulterar IMEI e desmontar celulares para reaproveitamento de peças;

Núcleo 4 (comercialização) : pessoas e empresas suspeitas de revender aparelhos e componentes, inclusive com documentação fiscal e circulação empresarial que dariam aparência regular aos produtos.

O caminho dos celulares roubados em SP — Foto: Arte/g1

Na prática, a tese dos investigadores aponta que o crime só continua compensando porque existe uma rede pronta para absorver rapidamente o aparelho roubado, apagar seus rastros e fazê-lo voltar ao mercado.

A investigação parte de um dado que já vinha chamando a atenção das autoridades: São Paulo concentra uma fatia expressiva dos roubos e furtos de celulares do país.

Segundo o documento do Gaeco, com base em dados do Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, o Brasil registrou 95 roubos e furtos de celulares por hora em 2025, sendo que o estado e capital paulista concentrariam cerca de 20% de todos os casos.

No recorte da cidade, o inquérito cita que São Paulo teve 154.058 celulares roubados ou furtados em 2025, média de 17 por hora. Desse total, apenas cerca de 10 mil foram devolvidos aos donos. Para os investigadores, esse percentual baixo de recuperação indica justamente a existência dessa estrutura eficiente para nutrir o crime.

A região da Rua Guaianases, em Santa Ifigênia e Campos Elíseos, aparece no inquérito como um dos principais polos de recepção imediata de celulares subtraídos. O local já vinha sendo mencionado em operações policiais há anos.

Segundo o material do MP, apenas em pesquisas feitas em sistemas policiais com referência à Rua Guaianases foram localizados mais de 500 registros de ocorrência envolvendo celulares em pouco mais de dois anos. Outro ponto considerado decisivo foi a repetição dos sinais de rastreamento.

Vítimas de crimes distintos, sem relação entre si, indicaram que seus aparelhos terminaram na mesma região, especialmente nas ruas Guaianases, Aurora e Timbiras.

Para o MP, essa concentração sugere que a área funciona como um "centro logístico": é ali que os celulares chegam, são guardados por pouco tempo e, depois, seguem para outras etapas da cadeia.

A investigação descreve dois grandes fluxos de abastecimento dessa engrenagem criminosa:

O primeiro envolve aparelhos levados em roubos com violência ou em furtos mediante quebra de vidro de veículos , que depois acabam localizados na região da 25 de Março, especialmente no Shopping Mundo Oriental e na Galeria Pagé.

O segundo tem como origem grandes eventos, festivais, shows e aglomerações públicas , com a Rua Guaianases sendo a protagonista. Entre os eventos citados na apuração estão Lollapalooza, Parada do Orgulho LGBT+, Virada Cultural, The Town, Tomorrowland e Só Track Boa.

Segundo o inquérito, nesses ambientes os criminosos agiriam com divisão de tarefas entre “batedores” e “recolhedores”. Os primeiros furtam; os outros recebem o aparelho rapidamente para acelerar o escoamento e reduzir o risco de flagrante.

Depois que o aparelho chega aos receptadores, começa uma etapa considerada estratégica pela investigação, com a atuação dos chamados “icloudeiros”, os especialistas em romper as proteções do celular.

A função deles, segundo o MP, é eliminar o vínculo entre o aparelho e o dono original. Isso pode incluir:

Alteração do IMEI, o número que identifica o aparelho perante as operadoras.

O objetivo inicial, segundo a investigação, nem sempre é vender o aparelho de imediato. Antes disso, os criminosos tentariam explorar o conteúdo digital da vítima ao acessar aplicativos bancários, contas pessoais e outros serviços para fazer PIX , empréstimos e fraudes financeiras.

articles.title: Ukraine's drone strikes Russian energy infra 3,000 km away from the borders
articles.summary: International News: A drone attack sparked a fire at an industrial facility in Novy Urengoy, a city just south of the Arctic circle and considered Russia's unofficial gas.
articles.body: A drone attack sparked a fire at an industrial facility in Novy Urengoy, a city just south of the Arctic circle and considered Russia's unofficial gas capital, marking the first such strike on the country's gas-producing heartland, regional Governor Dmitry Artyukhov said. The facility sits roughly 3,000 kilometres from the Ukrainian border in northwestern Siberia, a region holding an estimated 26.5 trillion cubic metres of gas reserves, enough to cover global demand for more than six years. Gazprom, which once exported gas from this region to Western Europe before ties collapsed after Russia's 2022 invasion.According to Ukraine's Special Operations Forces, as reported by the Kyiv Independent, the September 9 strike marks Kyiv's deepest attack into Russian territory since the war began, hitting a natural gas facility 3,200 kilometres from the border. It follows a pattern of expanding long-range strikes, Ukraine has hit an oil refinery in Omsk, nearly 2,500 kilometres away, and targeted refineries in Perm Oblast, over 1,500 kilometres from the border, in the past three months. Thus taking away the role of aircraft and missiles in the realm of precision long range strikes.Iran's Shahed drones offer another clear example of this shift. Cheap to build but capable of flying up to 2,000 kilometres, these drones have let Tehran project power well beyond its borders, striking Israel, Gulf states and even the UK's RAF Akrotiri base in Cyprus, some 1,100 kilometres away. The physical damage from these strikes has often been limited, but the message wasn't, Iran can hit distant targets without risking pilots or expensive missiles, using sheer volume to complicate even sophisticated air defences.India is moving down a similar path. The Army has inducted over a hundred indigenous kamikaze drones, the Peacekeeper or Agniveg, built for high-speed precision strikes on command centres and radar sites, alongside existing Harpy and Harop systems. The Air Force, meanwhile, is co-developing long-range kamikaze drones with domestic industry to cut dependence on foreign components, particularly Chinese ones, with systems like the Sheshnag, targeting a 1,000-kilometre range, currently under development.These developments explain why drones are increasingly seen as strategic weapons in their own right. They can strike far beyond the frontlines, disrupt energy infrastructure, and be deployed en masse thanks to their low cost relative to missiles, making them genuinely hard to defend against. For India, this isn't just about battlefield utility, drones are becoming a core part of military doctrine.

They are very pragmatic in their relationship, and they are as sincere as to be able to discuss in a very open and constructive way the most sensitive issues of our agenda and our bilateral relations. So, those are policy and security, economy and finance, and cultural and humanitarian contexts. So, we are supporting the idea of inviting new countries to join different formats within BRICS," he noted.India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13, 2026. articles.title: In 2021, an Illinois grain farmer put a 499-foot wind turbine on his 1,100-acre farm; it used just 0.1% of the land and the lease paid more than the crops that land could produce
articles.summary: US News: Discover how Illinois farmer Clayton Rosenberger transformed his land into a profitable venture by leasing a 499-foot wind turbine, considerably boosting his income while preserving crop production.
articles.body: Illinois farmer Clayton Rosenberger was approached by a wind company about putting a turbine on his land, which he and his wife did not like. The turbine would be nearly 500 feet tall and would stand among the corn and soybean fields of their 1,100-acre farm in McLean County. Rosenberger was also concerned about what it would sound like and how it would affect his work. The financial calculation eventually changed his mind, since the turbine took about 0.1% of his farm, and the lease provided income that Rosenberger said more than compensated for the land taken out of production.The turbine occupies about an acreThe finished turbine stands 499 feet tall when one blade is positioned vertically, just one foot below the county's height limit. Its foundation is a large concrete structure buried deep beneath the field, and the bottom of the foundation extends about 12 feet below ground, with excavated soil packed back around the structure so that much of the concrete is no longer visible.Ambrook's 2025 reporting calculated the turbine's footprint, including the covered foundation and surrounding gravel, at about two-thirds of a football field. That amounts to roughly 0.1% of Rosenberger's 1,100 acres, and this relatively small footprint meant most of the farm remained available for crop production. Rosenberger could also farm around the turbine base, as the lease accounted for the disruption caused by construction and the loss of crop production around the structure. The turbine began operating around 2021, and by the time Ambrook interviewed Rosenberger in 2025, he said he had largely stopped noticing it.The numbers mattered more than the viewRosenberger's farm was already surrounded by wind turbines on neighboring properties, and he worked and plowed some of those farms even though he did not own them. He reconsidered the possibility of putting one on his own property once he realized turbines were going up nearby. Before signing, he and his wife drove to an existing wind farm and parked underneath a turbine, and found the sound to be less intrusive than expected.Rosenberger estimated that he would lose roughly 1.1 acres of farmland because of the turbine. Ambrook reported that the turbine's payments would replace the income from those acres and provide additional money. Rosenberger ultimately became the last landowner in the area to sign the lease for his part of the wind project, and the arrangement gave him a source of income that was less directly tied to crop yields. “I’m a self-employed farmer. I don’t have a 401-K. I don’t have a retirement plan, but now I do,” Rosenberger told Ambrook. Ambrook also reported that farmers who add turbines to their properties typically receive between $8,000 and $33,000 a year, and cited USDA research that covered wind-energy costs from 2011 to 2020.Farming continues around the turbineAmbrook cited another USDA study finding that 94% of farmland remained in agricultural use as its primary use between 2012 and 2017 after a turbine was placed on the property. Rosenberger's continues to plant and harvest crops around the turbine, and adjusts his machinery's path near the foundation.The turbine took about eight months to build, and large equipment had to move across the farm during installation, but once construction ended, however, Rosenberger could return to regular field operations. The turbine is operated by EDP Renewables, which leases the land. Rosenberger also said the company would compensate him for damage caused by incidents such as lightning strikes.Rosenberger said his township covers only about six square miles and has roughly 300 residents, and receives additional tax revenue from the wind project. He recalled that the township had struggled financially before the wind farm arrived and said the new revenue had helped pay for infrastructure and fire equipment. The turbine therefore occupies a small physical part of the farm while creating a separate income stream for the landowner.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2022, a hydrologist’s team launched 40 floating wetlands made from bamboo, foam and discarded materials across Nepal’s polluted Nagdaha Lake; after five months, native flowering plants cut nitrate by up to 94% and iron by 95%
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover how innovative floating wetlands made from bamboo and recycled materials are dramatically improving water quality in Nagdaha Lake, Nepal, reducing nitrate and iron levels by up to 94% and 95%, respectively.
articles.body: Nagdaha Lake, a small body of water in the Kathmandu Valley in the Lalitpur district, was once used by the locals for daily tasks, irrigation, and washing. Like many urban lakes in South Asia, it has been absorbing runoff from the nearby settlements for the past few decades, absorbing household waste, agricultural fertiliser, and seepage from grazing land until nutrient levels reached a point where the lake was choked with algae and deprived of oxygen. Over the years, local advocacy groups attempted several cleanup initiatives, but because the underlying nutrient load in the water was never truly eliminated, eutrophication kept coming back.A new form of intervention came at the end of 2022, when a hydrologist and her team of researchers set out to see if the lake could effectively be given its own artificial root system. Dr. Soni M. Pradhanang, a hydrologist at the University of Rhode Island, was one of the collaborators on the project, which was led by Professor Sadhana Pradhanang. The design of 40 floating platforms made from bamboo frames, foam layers and matting, using recycled or locally sourced materials where possible.Transforming waste materials into a functional filterFloating treatment wetland is a horticultural concept rather than an engineering one; however, the chemistry beneath is quite advanced. The underside of the raft is covered by a dense, tangled surface of hanging roots, which provides a perfect habitat for biofilm, a thin layer of bacteria that thrives in the root zone. Together, the roots of the plants and the bacteria that live there pull dissolved nutrients straight from the surrounding water, pulling out chemicals such as nitrate and phosphate that would otherwise feed algal blooms.Because the rafts float on the water surface, their submerged root networks remain in direct contact with the water column rather than sitting on the lakebed.The project, funded through the Asia Pacific Network for Global Change Research, deliberately used discarded and low-cost materials to keep the approach replicable in communities with limited environmental budgets. The rafts were built and installed by local youth groups and volunteers along with the study team. For buoyancy they used styrofoam rescued from packaging, and for the structural frame they used bamboo. The project also involved local youth groups and volunteers in preparing and installing the rafts, since their visible presence gave residents and local government officials a tangible way to observe and understand a pollution remediation technology that might otherwise have remained an abstract research exercise.What the monitoring data showed after months in the waterThe team's researchers regularly monitored the water around the rafts to see how nutrient and metal concentrations changed over time, and the results after a few months of operation were stunning. Field monitoring revealed nitrate reductions up to ninety-four percent and a reduction of about ninety-five percent in dissolved iron levels in the treated parts of the lake. A separate 2025 study of polluted Hanumante River water in Nepal found nitrate removal rates of about 86% to 88% in floating treatment wetlands using several plant species, with some systems also removing more than 60% of iron.Not everything with the project went so easily, and that in itself is a helpful reminder that ecological engineering is not a linear process. The team had to replant hundreds of specimens after one of the two plant species withered during a seasonal transition and again the following year to keep the system operating. The project also produced a practical model that other sites can adapt.The regional FTWS project also involved collaborators in Bangladesh and India, and its guidebook provides practical guidance for adapting the technology to different sites and countries.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Indian paratroopers train with US, Japan, France in major Indo-Pacific war games
articles.summary: News News: Indian troops along with soldiers from 20 other nations are taking part in one of Indo-Pacific's largest multinational military exercises in terms of .
articles.body: Indian troops along with soldiers from 20 other nations are taking part in one of Indo-Pacific's largest multinational military exercises in terms of countries involved The wargames called Exercise Super Garuda Shield 2026, is nearing its end in the Indonesian archipelago, according to local media. Running from August 31 to September 11, the annual exercise has brought together 4,743 personnel who working through 12 separate training modules at multiple sites across the island chain.India's contribution has come in the form of 40 paratroopers as per reports from Indonesia. The report also mentions that Indian soldiers along with American, New Zealand and Indonesian troops participated in a joint "Special Operation Forces (SOF) Flat Range Advance Shooting" drill at the Indonesian Army's Combat Training Center in Martapura, South Sumatra. In all, 270 personnel took part in this active firing event along with 110 Indonesian troops, 80 American troops, 45 from New Zealand and 40 Indian soldiers, running through advanced live-fire drills designed to sharpen marksmanship, combat effectiveness and coordination in joint operational scenarios. The exercise wrapped up without incident.Beyond the shooting range, Indian troops also featured in the exercise's airborne segment. Indian paratroopers joined their Indonesian, American, Japanese and French counterparts in a static-line parachute exercise in which jumps were conducted from low altitudes of 1,200 feet over the Baturaja landing area in South Sumatra, one of several joint training activities designed to test how well partner militaries can operate together on short notice, as per Jakarta.Indonesian Armed Forces Commander General Agus Subiyanto said the broader exercise is meant to test operational readiness, deepen defence diplomacy and sharpen partner militaries' ability to respond to emerging security challenges, a description that captures just how far Super Garuda Shield has grown beyond a routine bilateral drill. Besides India, Indonesia and the US, participating nations this year include Australia, Japan, France, UK, Canada, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand and several other regional and partner countries, as per Indonesian media.For India, the exercise fits into a much bigger picture of strengthening ties with Indonesia under the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Jakarta has recently procured India's BrahMos supersonic cruise missile and become the first export customer for the Astra air-to-air missile, both signs of how far the defence relationship between the two countries has come. New Delhi and Jakarta also increasingly see eye to eye on maritime security and freedom of navigation across the Indo-Pacific, particularly around the strategically vital Malacca Strait. Multinational exercises like Super Garuda Shield continue to give India and its regional partners a working platform to build on that cooperation, one live-fire drill and parachute jump at a time.

articles.title: In 2023, Seville adapted a 3,000-year-old underground water technique to cool a renovated amphitheatre; the system uses solar power, water and underground cooling
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In a bold move against soaring temperatures, Seville has innovatively revived the ancient qanat system, cooling air in an abandoned amphitheatre with a temperature drop from 104°F to 63°F using solar-powered technology.
articles.body: Seville regularly experiences extreme summer heat, with temperatures frequently approaching 40 degrees Celsius. The Andalusian capital frequently experiences temperatures close to 40 degrees Celsius, or roughly 104 degrees Fahrenheit. Officials there have formally begun naming and categorising heatwaves, just as meteorologists do with hurricanes. A group of engineers and researchers in Seville concluded that a method created thousands of years ago might help address a pressing issue in a climate that scientists predict will only become harsher.That method is the qanat, a network of subterranean tunnels that Persian farmers invented some 3,000 years ago to transport water through parched regions without losing it to evaporation. A project called CartujaQanat has adapted this ancient engineering for a public square and a renovated amphitheatre on a former Expo site on the Isla de la Cartuja. It uses solar power, buried pipes, and the earth's naturally stable temperature to draw cool air up from below ground while the surface bakes overhead.How Seville adapted an ancient irrigation method for coolingThe original Persian qanats relied on gravity and the depth of the tunnels. Persian engineers finally recognised that vertical shafts connected to these tunnels could carry both water and cooled air to the surface. Water went through tunnels that were excavated far enough below the surface to keep soil temperatures cool throughout the year. CartujaQanat reconstructs the same fundamental idea with contemporary materials and a closed water circuit. Water flows through rooftop solar panels and an outdoor aqueduct at night before cooling in underground tanks with stable ground temperatures and cooler night air. During the day, solar-powered pumps force the same water through pipes placed in front of fans, creating an air current that is released into the amphitheatre and plaza through tiny holes in the steps and floor. Engineers working on the project said that the system can lower ground and ambient temperatures at the site by as much as 10 degrees Celsius. The system uses the thermal stability of underground soil and water to cool air before releasing it into the occupied space.Why depth and darkness matter more than machineryUnlike a conventional air conditioner, the system relies on underground thermal storage, water circulation and solar-powered equipment rather than refrigerants and compressors. The site itself sits two metres underground, with a white ceiling that reflects heat and columns and vegetation around it to help keep the temperature down even when the active pumping system is not functioning. Related research on earth-air-water heat-exchanger systems has found that nighttime cooling can lower soil temperatures and help maintain cooler conditions into the next day. That is precisely why the project’s directors say it is fundamentally different from a domestic air conditioner: the entire process depends on solar electricity and the physical properties of soil and water, not refrigerants or compressors. The initiative required substantial investment and combined European urban-innovation funding with support from local institutions. The project combined European urban-innovation funding with support from local institutions.Other hot cities are now watching the project carefully as a modelSeville’s experiment addresses a combination of extreme heat and dense urban development that affects cities across the Mediterranean and other hot regions. Recently, Indian cities have increasingly named and recorded heatwaves, matching the institutional seriousness that Seville initially devoted to the problem. The CartujaQanat project demonstrates that some of the oldest engineering solutions humans developed for arid climates, refined with modern solar power and monitoring rather than replaced by them, may still have a meaningful role to play as summers grow hotter and city budgets for climate adaptation remain limited. The CartujaQanat project shows how underground water infrastructure, solar energy and thermal storage can be combined in a public space to reduce heat exposure without relying entirely on conventional air conditioning.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: AI, quantum navigation & drone swarms: China’s J-50 aims to ‘leapfrog’ fighter technology
articles.summary: International News: China’s next-generation stealth fighters are being designed with advanced autonomous capabilities that could allow them to fly without a pilot, naviga.
articles.body: China’s next-generation stealth fighters are being designed with advanced autonomous capabilities that could allow them to fly without a pilot, navigate without satellite signals and control large groups of drones, according to new research by Chinese military aircraft designers.The research comes from the Shenyang Aircraft Design & Research Institute, linked to the development of the aircraft widely known as the J-50.A paper led by the institute’s chief flight-control designer, Zhang Dong, describes a “leapfrog transformation” in next-generation fighter technology, aimed at moving rapidly to more advanced capabilities instead of developing them step by step.It describes concepts including automatic control if a pilot is incapacitated, quantum navigation when satellite signals are unavailable, and fighter aircraft working with drones for attack, reconnaissance and protection missions.What does the “leapfrog” technology mean?The research points to a major shift in how China wants its next-generation fighters to operate. Instead of relying entirely on a pilot to control the aircraft, the designers are exploring systems that could allow the fighter to take over some tasks automatically and continue operating in difficult combat situations.One example is autonomous flight. If a pilot becomes unconscious or faces an extremely heavy workload, the aircraft could automatically take over control and continue flying. This could help keep the fighter operational even when the pilot is unable to control it normally.The researchers are also looking at navigation without satellite signals. The paper discusses quantum navigation, which could help an aircraft determine its position when systems such as GPS are unavailable or have been disrupted. This is important in a conflict because an enemy could attempt to jam or disable satellite-based navigation.Another major part of the concept is drone teaming. A manned fighter could work with a large number of drones, with the drones taking on different roles such as attack, reconnaissance and protection. Their formation could also be reorganised depending on the changing battlefield situation.China sixth generation fighter programmesChina is developing two major sixth-generation stealth-fighter programmes, represented by aircraft widely known as the J-36 and J-50. Both are still developmental aircraft, and Beijing has not officially confirmed these designations.The two prototypes first attracted global attention after appearing in flight tests in late 2024 and have since undergone further testing.The aircraft widely referred to as the J-36 is being developed by Chengdu Aircraft Corporation. Public images and analysis by defence experts indicate that it has a large, tailless design with three engines. Its size and configuration suggest a focus on long range, stealth and a large weapons payload, although its exact operational role has not been officially disclosed.The aircraft commonly called the J-50 is associated with the Shenyang Aircraft Design & Research Institute and is smaller than the J-36. It has a tailless, twin-engine design and has also undergone flight testing. Images of a later version showed the removal of the nose-mounted air-data boom used during earlier test flights, which analysts viewed as a possible sign of progress in the programme.The two sixth generation aircraft of China reflects two different approaches to sixth-generation airpower. The larger J-36 appears focused on range, payload and stealth, while the smaller J-50 could offer a different combination of agility, flexibility and potentially carrier operations. The parallel programmes also allow China to test different aerodynamic and technological solutions rather than committing to a single design from the beginning.

articles.title: West Virginia's restored elk herd is finally roaming farther; here's how a conservation comeback is changing the landscape
articles.summary: US News: Nearly a decade after elk were returned to West Virginia, the growing herd is beginning to venture beyond its familiar range, offering a new sign of h.
articles.body: Nearly a decade after elk were returned to West Virginia, the growing herd is beginning to venture beyond its familiar range, offering a new sign of how far the state’s ambitious wildlife restoration effort has come. The movement was highlighted by WV MetroNews, which reported in July that wildlife officials are seeing more elk explore beyond the Tomblin Wildlife Management Area in Logan County. The West Virginia Division of Natural Resources (WVDNR), meanwhile, says the restoration programme has brought the herd to about 130 animals and recorded at least 60 native calf births since the project began. One young female recently travelled north into Lincoln County near Harts Creek, spending time along a ridge and in a pasture on private farmland before returning to the Tomblin area. Wildlife officials were able to follow her movements through GPS telemetry. The journey is significant not because elk are suddenly spreading across the state, but because it shows individual animals are beginning to test the wider landscape available to them.From disappearing species to a growing herdElk once roamed widely across West Virginia but disappeared from the state by the late 1800s, largely because of overhunting and habitat loss. The modern restoration effort began after years of studies identified the southern coalfields as particularly suitable for elk. Large areas affected by surface mining had created open habitat, while relatively limited agricultural land reduced the likelihood of conflicts with farmers.In December 2016, the WVDNR released its first 24 elk at Tomblin Wildlife Management Area, marking the animals’ return after more than 140 years. The state subsequently added another 95 elk, 53 from Kentucky and 42 from Arizona, beginning in 2018. Additional releases in 2024 brought the estimated herd to about 130 animals. Since the programme began, at least 60 calves have been born in West Virginia.Why are the elk starting to wander?For now, Tomblin remains the centre of the herd’s range. But as the population grows, some animals are beginning to look for their own territory. GPS collars fitted to released elk, along with collars placed on previously unmarked animals, allow biologists to follow where they travel and how they use the landscape.The recent movements into Lincoln County therefore give researchers a glimpse of what the next phase of the restoration could look like. West Virginia’s designated Elk Management Area already covers about 2,845 square miles, spanning all of Logan, Mingo, McDowell and Wyoming counties and parts of Boone, Lincoln and Wayne counties.The state’s management strategy calls for officials to monitor elk movements around those boundaries and consider adjustments if the animals’ use of the wider landscape changes significantly.A conservation comeback that is also drawing visitorsThe return of elk has transformed the animals into both a conservation success and a growing tourism attraction. The WVDNR’s 2026 Elk Management Tours are scheduled to begin on September 13, with guided four-hour excursions continuing on weekends through October 24. The tours take visitors into elk country around Logan County, where park staff explain the animals’ behaviour, history and conservation.A viewing platform and education centre at Tomblin Wildlife Management Area, opened in 2025, have added another way for visitors to see the herd while learning about the restoration effort.The broader significance of the programme, however, lies beyond tourism. A species that vanished from West Virginia more than a century ago is now reproducing in the wild, establishing a home range and beginning to explore beyond it. For conservationists, those wandering elk may be among the clearest signs yet that the restoration is no longer simply about bringing the animals back, it is about watching them become part of the landscape again.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: Ukraine has once again attacked several infrastructure targets in Russia, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Thursday. Eight infrastructure objec...
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Zelensky announced that Ukraine has targeted eight infrastructure objects in Russia, including an oil refinery and a commercial port, in response to the ongoing conflict between the two countries.

A woman was killed in a Ukrainian drone strike in the Voronezh region, with two others injured, while falling drone debris from attacks in Dagestan and the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous District caused fires at port infrastructure and a theatre.

Ukraine has been using drones to counterattack against Russia, which has been engaged in a war with Ukraine for over four and a half years, with recent strikes targeting various regions in Russia.

Ukraine has once again attacked several infrastructure targets in Russia, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Thursday.

Eight infrastructure objects serving the Russian war effort were targeted, Zelensky wrote on social media.

He said an oil refinery in the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous District and a commercial port in the Russian Republic of Dagestan were hit. Facilities in the Moscow, Voronezh, Astrakhan and Bryansk regions were also targeted, Zelensky wrote, without providing details.

In the Voronezh region, a woman was killed in a Ukrainian drone strike in the city of Borisoglebsk, according to Governor Alexsandr Gusev. Two further people were injured, he said, adding that 19 Ukrainian drones had been intercepted over the region.

Dagestan's acting head of republic, Fyodor Shchukin, said that falling drone debris had started fires at port infrastructure and at a theatre in Makhachkala. There were no casualties, he said.

There were reports the previous day of a drone strike in the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous District in western Siberia, far from Ukraine. District Governor Dmitry Artyukhov said that falling drone debris had caused a fire at an unspecified industrial facility.

Russia has been waging a devastating war against Ukraine for more than four and a half years. As part of its defence effort, Ukraine has stepped up its counterattacks in recent months, primarily using drones.

articles.title: A Newport mansion is being restored with a staircase technique dating to the 1500s; instead of modern exposed fasteners, craftsmen lock the wooden steps together with mortises and wedges
articles.summary: US News: A stairway goes up to nowhere in a woodshop. No grand foyer at the bottom, no upper floor waiting at the top—just a full-scale helical structure surro.
articles.body: A stairway goes up to nowhere in a woodshop. No grand foyer at the bottom, no upper floor waiting at the top—just a full-scale helical structure surrounded by tools, machinery, and carefully prepared pieces of wood. But this unfinished staircase is also something much more: an intersection of centuries-old craftsmanship and contemporary engineering. Wondering what it is? Well, there is a stairway being built for the restoration of a historic home in Newport, Rhode Island. It is a Mark Richey Woodworking’s design and a revival of a late 16th century European method of building stairs, and uses modern computer modeling and manufacturing technology to achieve accurate results. According to an online report by Markrichey website, Newport is known for its grand Gilded Age homes, famously and somewhat facetiously referred to as “summer cottages.” Buildings like The Breakers, Miramar and Hammersmith Farm helped make the city a showcase of American architectural history. And this private residence being restored has undergone many renovations over the years. The current owners wanted to modernize the property but keep the character and craftsmanship that was part of the original design, states the online report.This went beyond just copying an old-fashioned look, as the architectural team also wanted construction techniques that would allow for the durability, precision and visual cleanliness of historic restoration. And that is when Mark Richey Woodworking was brought onto the project for its architectural millwork expertise and its knowledge of traditional woodworking methods.A 16th-century technique finds a modern revivalThe project’s heart is a dramatic helical staircase with laminated curved stringers and mortised-and-wedged treads and risers. As per reports, the technique originated in the construction of European staircases in the late 1500s, when wealthy homes and castles had elaborate staircases. This method does not use visible screws or nails to hold the finished treads and risers like many modern site-built stairs. Instead, each tread fits into a precisely cut recess—a mortise—and wooden wedges, glued in place on either side in the stringers, hold the components together. The result is a self-securing structure, each tread/riser assembly provides stability for the next. A hidden connection can also be used from below at the tongue and groove joint, but the finished walking surfaces are free of exposed fasteners.Made to move with the buildingHistoric buildings with wood framing are especially problematic, as they are never truly static. Wood expands and contracts with the seasons. Buildings settle, framing can shift over time. Face-fastened treads on notched stringers are common in conventional stairs and can cause gaps, squeaks and the look of filled screw or nail holes as these movements occur. The installation can be more difficult because the individual pieces often require a lot of fitting on the construction site. Another way to go is mortised-and-wedged construction. The technique aims to keep the joints tight by mechanically locking the wooden components together and to produce a strong, rigid assembly that can span considerable distances without additional support. The method offers both structural and esthetic benefits for a historic residence where appearance and longevity are equally important.Old craftsmanship comes back with technologyThe staircase is built in an old way of construction, but its creation is based on modern technology. Mark Richey Woodworking works with architects and builders during the design phase, helping to translate lofty architectural visions into components that can be manufactured. Engineers model complex shapes on 3D CAD systems and can check the design before starting fabrication. As per the online report, computer-controlled machinery produces components with the accuracy required for complex joinery, while skilled craftsmen do the fitting, laminating and finishing. This mix also reduces uncertainty at time of installation. The workshop can provide the staircase as a carefully engineered kit of parts, rather than shipping out unfinished components for extensive adjustment on the construction site.A full-scale rehearsal workshopFor especially complicated projects, the team is able to bring the actual environment of the staircase into the workshop. Full height temporary walls are constructed to the same radius and footprint as the actual stairwell. The complete helical stair for the Newport residence was preassembled in the shop and trucked to the property. This enabled the craftsmen to identify potential problems and check that the components fitted together before installation. And the result is a brilliant example of how historic craftsmanship does not necessarily mean something from the past. Mortises and wedges, a time-honored woodworking method, can be adapted to modern construction through CAD modeling, CNC machinery and precise hand-fitting, maintaining the character of a historic American home.Images Courtesy: MarkricheyCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Tax startup CEO allegedly faked CPA credentials and company revenue to raise $13.3 million; investors lost everything as funds paid for a home, Tesla and Caribbean wedding
articles.summary: US News: Federal agents arrested the former head of a Los Angeles tax compliance startup in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, as she was trying to board a luxury cruis.
articles.body: Federal agents arrested the former head of a Los Angeles tax compliance startup in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, as she was trying to board a luxury cruise ship. She has been charged with defrauding venture capital funds of more than $13 million (£10 million). Shiloh Luckey, 42, also known as Shiloh Johnson, was arrested on Sunday and later released on bond by a federal court in Florida, according to a press release from the United States Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California. Federal prosecutors allege that Luckey tricked investors into putting money into her now-defunct company, ComplYant App Inc, by falsely claiming she was a licensed certified public accountant (CPA) and making up the company’s recurring revenue figures. Prosecutors say that instead of building a genuine technology business, Luckey used investor money to fund an expensive lifestyle, including an Inglewood property, a Tesla and a luxury wedding on the Caribbean island of Anguilla.Arrest at the cruise terminalAccording to details released by the US Department of Justice, a federal grand jury in Los Angeles returned a 15-count indictment against Luckey on September 1. The charges include nine counts of securities fraud, three counts of wire fraud, one count of bank fraud and two counts of money laundering. The Federal Bureau of Investigation, which is leading the investigation, arrested Luckey in Florida before she could leave on vacation. She is expected to appear before a judge at the United States District Court in downtown Los Angeles in the coming weeks. If convicted on all charges, Luckey faces up to 30 years in federal prison for bank fraud, up to 20 years for each count of securities and wire fraud, and up to 10 years for each count of money laundering.Phantom clients and fake credentialsCourt documents describe what prosecutors say was a planned, multi-year fraud carried out in the Los Angeles technology sector. Luckey founded ComplYant in 2019 and marketed the app as a digital tool that helped small businesses manage complex tax requirements through a monthly subscription model. Between September 2020 and September 2023, Luckey pitched the software to venture capital investors. Prosecutors allege that she used false pitch decks, made-up financial updates and inflated cash balances to make ComplYant appear to be a fast-growing and highly profitable software company. To build trust with investors, Luckey repeatedly claimed that she was a licensed CPA with extensive experience in corporate accounting and tax strategy. However, federal prosecutors said in the indictment that Luckey had never been licensed as a CPA. Investors were allegedly misled by the false financial figures and claims about her qualifications. Venture capital groups eventually invested more than $13.3 million in the company.A house of cards built on bad checksFederal authorities also allege that Luckey carried out a check-kiting scheme in late 2022 to buy her home in Inglewood, California. During September and October 2022, Luckey allegedly wrote a $1.5 million check from a ComplYant bank account that did not have enough money to cover it. She deposited the check into another ComplYant account at a different bank and quickly wired the money to complete the property purchase before the banks detected the shortfall. When the first account fell deeply into the negative, prosecutors allege that Luckey used new money raised from venture capital investors to cover the missing funds.Complete loss for venture investorsBy September 2023, the company’s financial problems became impossible to hide. ComplYant faced severe cash shortages, suddenly stopped operating and eventually shut down completely. The collapse left venture capital investors facing total losses on their $13.3 million investments. Prosecutors allege that much of the money had already been spent on company expenses and Luckey’s personal lifestyle, including her Caribbean wedding. The case is being handled by Assistant United States Attorney Andrew M. Roach of the Major Frauds Section in Los Angeles. An indictment is a formal accusation of wrongdoing and does not mean the accused has been found guilty. Federal officials stressed that Luckey is presumed innocent unless and until she is proven guilty in court.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
